key_insight: Entrance-driven vortices in lab-scale DCMD cause Reynolds-number-dependent temperature polarization, and the bias can switch from stronger to weaker TP as flow rate increases.
engineering_relevance: Membrane distillation correlations and module comparisons must account for entrance geometry and inlet Reynolds number, because a single correction factor will not capture heat-transfer bias across operating conditions.
method: 3D CFD of direct-contact membrane distillation modules
Swept inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000
Varied side-chamber length and main-channel height to isolate geometry effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CFD results across multiple geometries and Reynolds numbers, showing vortex persistence, secondary-flow energy changes, and TP deviations relative to a straight-channel baseline.
watch_item: The findings are simulation-based, so transfer to real modules may depend on membrane properties, manufacturing tolerances, and experimental boundary conditions.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
